name: Polish Red Dog
description: Banking game: players bet without seeing their cards or the dealer's card that they hold a same-suit card higher than the dealer's upcard; winner is paid twice the bet from the pot. Also Stitch, Polski Pachuck.

content.text: Banking game: players bet without seeing their cards or the dealer's card that they hold a same-suit card higher than the dealer's upcard; winner is paid twice the bet from the pot. Also Stitch, Polski Pachuck.

Polish Red Dog is a variant of the Red Dog banking game family, similar to Slippery Sam but with fully blind betting: players bet without seeing either their own three cards or the dealer's card. It was described in Ostrow's Complete Card Player (1945) and reprinted in various later card-game books; alternative names include Stitch and Polski Pachuck.
Two to about eight; one is dealer (banker), others bet in turn.
Dealer puts up a fixed initial stake. Dealer deals three cards face down to each other player; players do not look at their cards until after betting.
